newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely firmer, still nervous.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely firmer, still nervous.

text.p: Gold led the precious metals into a narrow range on Tuesday apparently postponing any attempt to continue a breakout from recent lows, dealers said.
"It looks like anything above about $358.25 will be sold in to and buying will occur at about $356.20 which puts in its range," a dealer said, adding that business was quiet.
Bullion was fixed at $357.40 per ounce compared with $357.30 on Tuesday morning and $359.60 on Monday afternoon.
At the fixing a quiet Comex market was showing February gold one dollar weaker at $358.70.

U.S. December consumer price index (CPI) and retail sales data had no impact on the market after core CPI came in below November's increase at 0.1 percent versus a forecast gain of 0.2 percent. Retail sales were up 0.6 percent.
Dealers said the market was still trying to assess the psychological impact of Monday's announcement from the Dutch central bank that it had sold 300 tonnes of gold late last year.
"There has been psychological damage because of the Dutch sale. The feeling is, "Which one is next?'" the dealer said.
"The outlook doesn't look good. From a speculative point of view, the only reason to buy gold is if you think prices will go up. The central bank sales threaten the opposite," he said.
Trading activity had been quite active and fairly nervous earlier with gold trading up to $358 in Asia, then dropping to $356 in early Europe before a bounce took it up to around $357.
In the near term gold looked likely to retest the lows of last week when prices dipped below $354 an ounce, he added.
Another dealer referred to the statement from Hans Tietmeyer, chairman of the G10 central bank governors, that the G10 central banks had no intention of selling gold "for the time being."
"Many people in the market still feel that another central bank was selling late last year," a dealer said.
He added that offtake by fabricators and other consumers was much less than a year ago when prices were about $40 higher.
"They obviously think price will go down further otherwise they would be taking advantage now," he said.
Silver was unchanged at $4.71/$4.73 despite being under technical pressure to visit $4.62. Platinum was $0.50 lower at $362.00/$363.00 and palladium was down $0.35 at $120.75/$121.75.
